decision.buyer: Cooling and component suppliers (a hypothesis in #342; no customer demand or paid pilot is claimed).
decision.engineering_decision: Choose straight-microchannel dimensions and coolant flow for a single-phase copper cold plate on a 30 x 30 mm die with an axial hot spot, trading the hottest die temperature against pumping power.
decision.intended_use: Predict the heated-face peak temperature, its 30-segment profile along the flow, and the pressure drop of the declared OpenFOAM reference over the DEVELOPMENT population; agreement is with that model (the periodic interior of a straight-channel plate), not with a built plate.

pilots.note: The package reference against rung 6e and the fluid-model choice. The two REFERENCE_INVALID records are the cp-varying diagnostic, which fails the exact energy check by design (that is why the reference holds cp). A seventh, r = 3 hot-spot case was stopped by the operator; the pilot's refinements cover it.

#342's pilot shape: 8 ordinary and 4 difficult cases (screen edge, sharpest spot, highest pressure drop, highest Re) with 4 paired r = 3 refinements, from public draws of the DEVELOPMENT population; run on the owner's local host. An earlier attempt was stopped by the operator after about two minutes, with no records, to move it to a runner that outlives the session.

population.proposed: carbon.cold-plate.development-population.v1: independent uniform draws over the nine-input box, admitted when the closed-form model (with axial spreading) predicts a hottest wetted wall of at most 95 C and Re of at most 2,000 (about 84 % of the box). A proposed DEVELOPMENT population, not a ratified production one.

recommendation.basis: All 16 pilot cases ran OK with exact checks (mass 6.9e-10, energy 2.1e-6); the r = 2 reference's discretization (about 0.1 K, 0.33 K worst; Delta p within 1.6 %) is about a tenth of the conventional baseline's error. The pools are complete (400 TRAIN, 100 PRACTICE, 200 private, all OK) and both baselines are scored through the exam on the private pool: the conventional closed form 0.109 (peak 0.138, profile 0.149, pressure 0.041) and the generic kernel-ridge model 0.105 (0.118, 0.182, 0.016). The conventional model with axial spreading is a strong baseline; the generic learned model barely improves on it and is worse on the profile, so a useful surrogate must beat a physics-aware baseline, not a generic one.

reference.applicability: The declared box admitted by the population screen; fluid at most 99 C (the coolant model's end) and Re at most 2,000, both checked per case; the periodic interior only (no headers, manifolds, plate edges or spanwise heat maps). Discretization at r = 2: about 0.1 K on the peak for most cases, 0.33 K at the screen edge, and Delta p 0.9 to 1.6 % low (pilot refinements).
reference.licence: GPL-3.0 as published upstream; run on the operator host only; Carbon writes its inputs and reads its outputs; redistribution not reviewed
reference.model: Steady laminar conjugate heat transfer in the periodic cell (half channel, half fin) on the rungs' wall-graded mesh (r = 2, grading 4); PG25 from CoolProp 6.8.0 fits with viscosity, density and conductivity varying and heat capacity held at the inlet; copper C11000, k = 391; axial hot-spot flux as an OpenFOAM expression

unresolved: The generic learned baseline barely improves on the conventional model (private pool 0.105 against 0.109) and is worse on the profile; a physics-aware learned baseline is untested.
Spanwise heat-map variation, headers and manifolds need a multi-channel domain (about 50x the cost): the recorded v2 expansion.
Heat capacity is held at the inlet temperature (about 0.1 K on the peak, rung 7) to keep the energy check exact.
The inlet undershoot (up to 2.3 K, linearUpwind) is reported, not judged; a bounded scheme is untested.
Miner-path integration is CHALLENGE-COLD-PLATE-02; the registry entry stays RESERVED until then.
Every value above is a provisional DEVELOPMENT value; scientific, security and launch review are human-reserved.
